q1_issues.issue: The demonstrative subject "This" gets no symbol and no class atom, although the instruction set makes a witness plus its class atom mandatory for a pronoun with no antecedent (it -> the salient kind, else thing).
The clause's predication is unrepresented: the three atoms assert only the presupposed existence of a road and its end, so nothing in the parse records the claim the sentence actually makes.

q2_gaps: equative / identity copular clause whose complement is a definite description ("This is the end of the road") — Categorical statements covers only "X is a/an N" and "X is ADJ", and nothing says whether an identity is encoded by symbol reuse, by Member on the complement's head noun, or by some identity head
deictic "this"/"that" as a bare subject with no CONTEXT antecedent — the pronoun list covers he/she/they/it but not demonstratives
notes: PartOf for "the end of the road" is the right branch of the genitive test (an end is a portion of the road), and the literal reading is correctly preferred over the idiom since the literal one is coherent here.
